pride_data.title: Charting the dynamic trophoblast plasma membrane identifies LYN as a functional regulator of syncytialization (supplemental)
pride_data.projectDescription: The differentiation of placental cytotrophoblasts (CTBs) into the syncytiotrophoblast (STB) layer results in significant remodeling of the plasma membrane proteome. Here, we use a peroxidase-catalyzed proximity labeling strategy to quantitatively map the dynamic plasma membrane proteomes of CTBs and STBs. Coupled with mass spectrometry-based proteomics, we identify hundreds of plasma membrane proteins and observe quantitative changes in protein abundance throughout differentiation, including the upregulation of the plasma membrane-localized non-receptor tyrosine kinase LYN. We show that both siRNA-mediated knockdown and small molecule inhibition of LYN kinase function impairs CTB fusion and abrogates the expression of syncytialization markers, presenting a function for LYN outside of its canonical role in immunological signaling. Our results demonstrate the use of the proximity labeling platform to discover functional regulators within the plasma membrane and provide new avenues to regulate trophoblast differentiation.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: After proximity labeling, cells were lysed by sonication (Branson SFX250 sonicator; 15 ms on, 40 ms off, 15% amplitude) in PBS buffer. Protein concentration was determined by the DC™ Protein Assay (Bio-rad), and lysates were normalized to approximately 350 µg in 500 µL PBS. Protein was precipitated overnight (-20°C in 2 mL of cold methanol (Thermo Scientific Chemicals) and pelleted by centrifugation (3,200 xg, 10 min). The supernatant was carefully aspirated, and the pellet was washed with 1 mL of cold methanol (Thermo Scientific Chemicals). Protein was pelleted again then resuspended in 500 µL of 6 M urea (Supelco) and 0.2% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) (Sigma-Aldrich). Sample was reduced with 50 µL of a mixture of 100 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) (Thermo Scientific Chemicals) and 300 mM potassium carbonate (Thermo Scientific Chemicals) in PBS. Samples were incubated at 37°C for 30 minutes then alkylated with 70 µl of 400 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) (Sigma-Aldrich) (30 min, RT, protected from light). Sample was diluted with 5.5 mL of PBS and brought to 0.2% SDS. 1 mL of Pierce™ Streptavidin Agarose beads (Thermo Scientific™) were washed twice with 10 mL of PBS then resuspended to approximately 2 mL in PBS. 200 µl of the resuspended beads were added to each sample and incubated at room temperature for 1.5 hours while rotating. Beads were then washed with 5 mL of 0.2% SDS in PBS, 5 mL of PBS, and 5 mL of 100 mM tetraethylammonium bromide (TEAB), pH 8.5 (Thermo Scientific™). Beads were transferred from 15 mL tubes to Eppendorf® LoBind tubes using two 500 µl washes with 100 mM TEAB, pH 8.5. Beads were pelleted, supernatant aspirated, and sample resuspended with 2 µg of sequencing grade modified porcine trypsin (Promega) in 100 mM TEAB, pH 8.5 with 1 mM CaCl2. Samples were digested overnight at 37°C. Beads were pelleted and supernatant retained in new Eppendorf® LoBind tubes. Beads were washed with 100 µl of TEAB pH 8.5 to ensure complete transfer of released peptides. Sample was brough to 30% acetonitrile (ACN) (Fisher Chemical™). TMT10plex™ Isobaric Label (Thermo Scientific™) tandem mass tags (TMT) were added to each sample and incubated at 37°C for one hour with occasional vortex. Reaction was quenched with 6 µl of 5% hydroxylamine (Sigma-Aldrich) (15 minutes, RT). Sample was acidified with 4 µL of formic acid (Fisher Chemical™) and dried by vacuum concentration. The samples are then combined by reconstituting the first sample with 200 µl of 5% ACN and 0.5% TFA (Thermo Scientific Chemicals) in water. The resuspended first sample was subsequently transferred to each tube with dried peptide from the experiment to ensure all TMT labeled samples were combined. This process was repeated with 100 µl of 5% ACN and 0.5% TFA in water to ensure complete recovery of all samples. Samples were desalted using the Pierce™ Peptide Desalting Spin Columns (Thermo Scientific™) per manufacturer instructions. Eluted sample was dried by vacuum concentration. For MS runs, sample was resuspended in 20 µl of 0.1 % formic acid in water, underwent a hard spin, and the supernatant was retained to load onto the instrument.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS-based proteomics experiments were designed with three technical replicates of proximity labeled CTB and STB cells and two technical replicates of the negative controls lacking APEX2 in both CTB and STB cells. Three biological replicates were performed, resulting in a total of 30 samples. The number of samples was chosen within budgeted allowance; an a priori power analysis was not performed. Data were processed in Proteome Discoverer version 2.4 (Thermo Scientific™) with the SEQUEST HT homo sapiens sequence database (42,358). Peptides were generated with trypsin with one missed cleavage site allowed (no semi-tryptic peptides were included). Carbamidomethyl modification of cysteines and the TMT10plex of lysines and the peptide N-terminus were considered in fixed modifications. Oxidation of residues was considered in variable modifications. The fragment ion mass tolerance was 0.6 Da, and the mass tolerance was 10 ppm. The false discovery rate was 1%. Identified proteins were filtered for 2 or more unique peptides, and all keratins were removed from the dataset. To filter for plasma membrane proteins, a protein was excluded if it did not have any one of the following Uniprot subcellular location annotations or Uniprot cellular compartment GO annotations: "basolateral cell membrane”, "cell membrane", "secreted", "cell junction", "apical cell membrane", "extracellular space”, "apical plasma membrane", "basolateral plasma membrane", "extracellular region", "tight junction", "integral component of membrane", "cell surface", and "extracellular matrix". Data from all three experiments were combined and normalized to the abundance of the protein pyruvate carboxylase (PC, Uniprot accession #P11498), which natively includes a biotin cofactor. The abundance values were converted to log2(Y). Statistical comparisons between groups were performed with GraphPad Prism software (GraphPad) using an unpaired student’s t test. Results are presented as an average fold change on the x-axis and the p-value on the y-axis. Significance was determined to have a p-value of less than 0.05. The p-value is reported on the y-axis as -log(p-value), so statistical significance is assigned with values greater than 1.30.
